Committee: County and Municipal Government
Sponsor: Ingram
Analyst: Vee Mosely
Date: 02/09/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 120 as introduced could increase the administrative costs of local boards of education by an undetermined amount to establish policies requiring each public K-12 school to broadcast "The Star-Spangled Banner" at school-sanctioned sporting events and at least once a week during school hours.
Reed Ingram, Chair
County and Municipal Government

Committee: County and Municipal Government
Sponsor: Ingram
Analyst: Vee Mosely
Date: 02/19/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 120 as introduced limits the authority of a municipality or county to regulate the installation and use of a battery-charged fence as defined in this act which could decrease potential receipts to municipal and county general funds by an undetermined amount dependent on the level at which the county or municipality would charge permits or fees for installation or use of a battery-charged fence.
Reed Ingram, Chair
County and Municipal Government

Committee: Education Policy
Sponsor: Baker
Analyst: Daniel Davenport
Date: 02/10/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 93 as amended and reported by the Committee on Education Policy allows Tier II plan members of the Teachers Retirement System (RSA) to (1) convert accrued sick leave into creditable service and (2) withdraw from service after the completion of at least 30 years of creditable service.
In addition, for pay dates beginning on or after October 1, 2021, the bill increases the member contribution rate for Tier II plan members from 6% currently to 6.75% per payroll period; and increases the member contribution rate for Tier II correctional officers, firefighters, or law enforcement officers from 7% currently to 7.75% per payroll period.
According to the actuary for the Retirement Systems of Alabama (RSA), this bill would increase total TRS employer contributions by an estimated $5.1 million for FY 2023, with approximately $3.0 million being paid from the Education Trust Fund appropriation to agencies/entities through the increase in the employer contribution rate for Tier II and Tier I by 0.05% and 0.08%, respectively, due to the increase in the unfunded liability rate associated with the change.
Terri Collins, Chair
Education Policy
